topic: Maintaining useful learner starting paths through a course-library revision
task: Use the supplied private simulated operating material to decide what, if anything, needs attention after this library revision. Preserve uncertainty and source identity. The existing manual method remains available; no new tool, supplier, subscription, or automation is required. A useful response may include selective action, clarification, retaining the incumbent, or rejecting unnecessary work.

sources.text: Previous library snapshot: foundations r2, 8 minutes, text, no prerequisites; charts r3, 12 minutes, captioned video, foundations recommended; field-notes r1, 15 minutes, text, no prerequisites; analysis r2, 25 minutes, interactive desktop exercise, charts required. These are four synthetic library entries, not a measured catalog or real users.

Current library snapshot: foundations r2 unchanged; charts r4, 18 minutes, video, foundations listed as required, caption review pending; field-notes r1 is archived and no longer listed for new starters, but its stable entry remains available to existing learners; observation r1, 10 minutes, text, is a possible alternative to field-notes, equivalence not evaluated; analysis r2 unchanged and still points to charts without a revision pin.

Three synthetic queued starting paths: learner-case-1 has an 8-minute mobile break and has foundations r2 assigned; learner-case-2 has a 15-minute text-only session and already has field-notes r1 assigned; learner-case-3 has completed foundations r2, has 15 minutes today, needs captions, and was assigned charts r3 before the release. No completion or satisfaction evidence exists for these assignments.

Catalog editor note for r8: charts now introduces an exercise using concepts from foundations, so the catalog marks it required. The author note in the charts package still calls foundations recommended. No one has resolved that discrepancy. Caption review pending means not yet verified, not proof of inaccessibility.

Library policy: archived entries can remain usable for existing assignments; removal from discovery does not authorize breaking old links or silently substituting content. New starters should not be sent an archived entry without explaining its status. Preserve the original assignment record when changing a recommendation.

Current manual method: an operator compares the two catalog exports, looks at affected assignments, and writes a short change note. It has no demonstrated reliability or cost advantage over a proposed helper, but requires no new account or ongoing subscription. The source exports can be reused. Some releases change only titles or ordering; these need not create learner-facing work.

The simulated learning team values a startable, appropriate next step more than covering the entire library. It dislikes automatic changes that erase context. It has not committed to buying anything. There is no emergency deadline or promise of a reply. The current sample cannot establish how often these problems recur.

Operator-seeded private scenario, not organic customer history. The dataset is sufficient to reason about this release and three hypothetical assignments, not to infer actual learning gains, enjoyment, demand, a market size, or a generalized product requirement. A supplier may decline the problem or ask for additional evidence.
